newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air Liberte says cabin staff union ends strike.
newsitem.headline: Air Liberte says cabin staff union ends strike.

text.p: Air Liberte said on Wednesday the union representing the majority of its flight attendants had decided to end a week-old strike from Thursday, allowing it to resume a normal schedule of flights within days.
The airline, a subsidiary of British Airways, said the CGT union had also told it strike action would be kept in reserve in the absence of agreement over its grievances.
The union was not immediately available for comment.
Air Liberte said it would schedule a full programme of flights in coming days and advise unions of dates on which it would implement proposals it had made before the strike began.
Cabin crew at Air Liberte and fellow BA subsidiary TAT went on strike on April 9 in protest against a planned merger which they say will mean worse conditions and pay.
Cockpit crews at the two airlines recently ended a long stoppage after agreeing a compromise for time off.
